the application of model breads in the study of the interactions between AX-protein and starch.
the possibility to use model bread in the examination of the interactions between AX, protein and starch in rye bread.
the possibility of using a model bread baking to examine the interactions of AX and proteins in rye bread.

AX-protein interactions are the most significant factor determining the structure of the crumb of the rye bread baked from the model dough.

the application of a model rye baking system allowed for the identification of the optimal composition of the model mix, and the determination of the molecular mass of AX-protein complexes in the model rye bread crumb.
the model bread baking method is an excellent tool for the study of AX-protein interactions.

the AX-protein complexes of higher molecular mass, isolated from the crumb, are responsible for the strength of bread crumb structure.
AX-protein complexes in the bread crumb are formed during baking and they have the greatest influence on the bread structure.

the application of a model bread baking in combination with a size exclusion chromatography allowed to determine the optimum ratio of the components of the dough, which would be the best for the formation of the most stable complexes between AX and protein.

the model bread baking method can be used to investigate the interactions of AX and protein in rye flour.
